Rashi on Gittin 43a:10:1.hebrew: בקדושין - אמרינן: "התקדשי לחציי" — מקודשת, "חצייך מקודשת לי" — אינה מקודשת; הכא מי הוי קדושין או לא:
Rashi on Gittin 43a:10:1.english: In [tractate] Kiddushin - we say: [If a man says to a woman,] "Be betrothed to half of me," she is betrothed; [if he says,] "Half of you is betrothed to me," she is not betrothed; here [in the case of a half-slave half-freeman], is it [a valid] betrothal or not?

Rashi on Gittin 43a:11:1.hebrew: כשעשאו טריפה - דהוה ליה כמאן דקטליה, ויהב ליה לנפשיה:
Rashi on Gittin 43a:11:1.english: When it made him a tereifa - for it is as though it killed him, and he gives [it] to himself:

Rashi on Gittin 43a:12:1.hebrew: ועוד כופר הוא כו' - דבשלמא קנס, דלא כתיב ביה מיתה אלא נגיחה, שנאמר "אם עבד יגח השור וגו'" (שמות כ״א:ל״ב), איכא לאוקמיה כשעשאו טריפה; אבל בכופר של בן חורין כתיב "והמית איש או אשה":
Rashi on Gittin 43a:12:1.english: And furthermore, it is ransom, etc. - For granted, [regarding] the fine [for a slave], where death is not written concerning it, but rather goring — as it is stated: "If the ox gores a slave, etc." (Exodus 21:32) — one can establish it [as referring to a case] where [the ox] rendered him a tereifa; however, regarding the ransom of a free person, it is written: "and it killed a man or a woman":

Rashi on Gittin 43a:12:2.hebrew: ראוי ליטול - דפלגא לאו בר קנסא הוא, אלא בר כופר:
Rashi on Gittin 43a:12:2.english: It is fitting [for heirs] to take - For the [free] half is not subject to a fine, but rather [is subject] to ransom:

Rashi on Gittin 43a:12:3.hebrew: ואין לו - שהרי מת, ויורשים אין לו שיגבו, וזה המזיק זכה במה שבידו. ולעולם בשמת, וה"ק: נותן חצי קנס לרבו, וחצי כופר ראוי לינתן ליורשיו אם היו לו יורשין:
Rashi on Gittin 43a:12:3.english: And he does not have [heirs] - for he has died, and he has no heirs to collect [it], so this damager retains what is in his possession. Indeed, [it refers] to a case where he died, and this is what it is saying: he gives half the fine to his master, and the half-ransom is fit to be given to his heirs if he had heirs:

Rashi on Gittin 43a:15:1.english: [He] placed an interpreter before him - He stationed a spokesman before him to expound again:

Rashi on Gittin 43a:15:2.hebrew: והמכשלה הזאת - כלומר, כך התחיל בדרשא: מקרא כתוב "והמכשלה הזאת תחת ידיך" — באנשי ירושלים שפסקה תורה מהם, והיו שואלין לחבריהם: "שמלה לך קצין תהיה לנו והמכשלה הזאת תחת ידיך"; כלומר, דברים שמכוסין כשמלה שלך הן, שאתה בקי בהן, אמור לנו ותהיה קצין, והמכשלה הזאת — דברי תורה, שאין אדם עומד על אמיתתן עד שיכשל בהן להורות טעות ויכלימוהו, והוא נותן לב ומבין — תחת ידיך הן; אף אני נכשלתי בהוראתי וחוזרני בי:
Rashi on Gittin 43a:15:2.english: And this stumbling-block - that is to say, this is how he began [his] homiletical exposition: A verse is written, "And let this stumbling-block be under your hand" — [speaking] of the people of Jerusalem, from whom Torah had ceased, and they would ask their fellows: "You have a garment, you shall be our ruler, and let this stumbling-block be under your hand." That is to say: matters that are covered like a garment are yours, for you are expert in them; tell [them to] us and you shall be [our] ruler; and "this stumbling-block" — [meaning] words of Torah, whose truth a person does not comprehend until he stumbles in them by issuing an erroneous ruling and they put him to shame, and he takes [it] to heart and understands — are under your hand. [So too,] I have stumbled in my ruling, and I retract.

Rashi on Gittin 43a:16:1.hebrew: ואם לחשך אדם לומר - תשובה לדבר זה, מאותה ששנינו במס' כריתות (יא.): "והפדה לא נפדתה" דשפחה חרופה, איזו זו? זו פדויה ואינה פדויה, חציה שפחה וחציה בת חורין המאורסה לעבד עברי. והוא הדין לכל ישראל, אלא אורחא דמלתא נקט, משום דעבד עברי מותר בשפחה:
Rashi on Gittin 43a:16:1.english: And if a person whispers to you, saying - [raising] an objection to this [statement] from that which we learned in Tractate Keritot (11a): "[And] she has not been redeemed" regarding a designated maidservant — which [woman] is this? This is one who is redeemed and not redeemed, a half-maidservant half-free woman who is betrothed to a Hebrew slave. And the same law applies to any Israelite; rather, [the Tanna] stated the usual case, because a Hebrew slave is permitted [to cohabit] with a maidservant:

Rashi on Gittin 43a:16:2.english: Apparently she can be betrothed - [This is inferred] from [the fact] that it teaches "betrothed":

Rashi on Gittin 43a:16:3.english: Say to him - Do you really think that it is an actual betrothal?

Rashi on Gittin 43a:16:4.hebrew: כלך אצל רבי ישמעאל - דאמר התם: "דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם", ובשפחה כנענית שלא נפדית כלל קמשתעי קרא:
Rashi on Gittin 43a:16:4.english: Go to Rabbi Yishmael - who says there: "The Torah spoke in the language of human beings," and [thus] the verse is speaking of a Canaanite maidservant who was not redeemed at all:

Rashi on Gittin 43a:16:5.hebrew: המאורסה לעבד עברי - וכי שפחה כנענית גמורה בת קדושין היא? הא חמורה בעלמא היא, עם הדומה לחמור:
Rashi on Gittin 43a:16:5.english: Betrothed to a Hebrew slave - Is a full Canaanite maidservant capable of betrothal? Why, she is merely [like] a she-donkey, "a people resembling a donkey":

Rashi on Gittin 43a:17:1.hebrew: מיוחדת - וגזירת הכתוב היא דמחייב עלה אשם, הואיל וייחדוה לעבד עברי המותר בה:
Rashi on Gittin 43a:17:1.english: Designated - And it is a scriptural decree that he is liable [to bring] a guilt-offering on her account, since they designated her for a Hebrew slave, who is permitted [to cohabit] with her:

Rashi on Gittin 43a:18:1.hebrew: וחזרה ונתקדשה לשמעון - אחיו, ובחיי ראובן, וראובן לא גירשה:
Rashi on Gittin 43a:18:1.english: And she went back and was betrothed to Shimon - his brother, and during Reuven's lifetime, and Reuven did not divorce her:

Rashi on Gittin 43a:1:1.hebrew: דלמא מודה - בב"ד קודם העדאת עדים, ומודה בקנס פטור:
Rashi on Gittin 43a:1:1.english: Perhaps he will admit - in court before the testimony of witnesses, and one who admits to a fine is exempt:

Rashi on Gittin 43a:3:1.hebrew: ויליד בית מה ת"ל - לענין אכילת תרומה: "ויליד ביתו הם יאכלו בלחמו"; יליד בית — בן שפחתו:
Rashi on Gittin 43a:3:1.english: "And one born in the house" — what does the verse mean [to teach] - Regarding eating terumah, [Scripture states]: "and those born in his house, they may eat of his bread" [Leviticus 22:11]; "one born in the house" [means] the son of his maidservant:

Rashi on Gittin 43a:4:1.hebrew: אילו כן - דלא כתיב אלא "קנין כספו הוא יאכל בו":
Rashi on Gittin 43a:4:1.english: If so - [meaning,] if only "the purchase of his money, he shall eat of it" were written:

Rashi on Gittin 43a:5:1.hebrew: אף קנין כסף אע"פ שאינו שוה כלום - כגון שנעשה מוכה שחין:
Rashi on Gittin 43a:5:1.english: So too, a monetary acquisition, even though he is not worth anything - For example, where he became afflicted with boils:

Rashi on Gittin 43a:6:1.english: Is there a slave that cannot be sold - [with regard to the penalty, even] for a perutah?

Rashi on Gittin 43a:6:2.hebrew: לקנסא - שאם יגחנו שור, יטול שלשים כסף:
Rashi on Gittin 43a:6:2.english: With regard to the penalty - That if an ox gores him, he [the buyer] collects thirty [shekels of] silver:

Rashi on Gittin 43a:6:3.hebrew: בטרפה - שאין משלמין עליו קנס, דגברא קטילא הוא:
Rashi on Gittin 43a:6:3.english: In [the case of] a tereifa - for one does not pay the penalty for him, since he is [considered] a dead man:

Rashi on Gittin 43a:7:1.hebrew: והא חזי למיקם קמיה - לשרתו, אע"פ שנחתכה רגלו למעלה מן הארכובה או ניקב קרום המוח, ראוי לשירות קל:
Rashi on Gittin 43a:7:1.english: But isn't he fit to stand before him - to serve him; even though his leg was severed above the knee or the membrane of the brain was punctured, he is [still] fit for light service:

Rashi on Gittin 43a:7:2.hebrew: במנוול - דמאיס, והוי נמי טרפה דלאו בר קנסא הוא:
Rashi on Gittin 43a:7:2.english: With [one who is] disgusting - who is repulsive, and he is also a tereifa, so that he is not subject to a fine:

Rashi on Gittin 43a:8:1.hebrew: אם תמצא לומר - כלומר, אי בעית למפשט מדקיימא לן "התקדשי לחציי מקודשת", לא דמי; דהתם בר חורין הוא וחזיא לכוליה, והכי קאמר לה: "אי בעינא נסיבנא אחריתי בהדיך", אבל הא לא חזיא לפלגא דעבדות דידיה:
Rashi on Gittin 43a:8:1.english: If you say - That is to say, if you wish to resolve [the dilemma] from what we have established [elsewhere, that if one says], "Be betrothed to half of me," she is betrothed — it is not comparable; for there he is a freeman and she is fit for all of him, and this is what he is saying to her: "If I wish, I will marry another [woman] alongside you," but this [woman] is not fit for his slave half:

Rashi on Gittin 43a:9:1.hebrew: ואם תמצא לומר חצייך מקודשת לי אינה מקודשת - ובעית למפשט הא מינה, דכי היכי דמקדש חצי אשה אינה מקודשת — הואיל דלא מצינן למימר דהכי קאמר לה דתנסיב אחרינא בהדי, דאיתתא לא חזיא לתרי, ואשתכח דפלגא הוא דקדיש — הכא נמי חצי איש שקידש לא הוו קידושין; לא דמי, דהתם שייר בקנינו, דהוה ליה לקדשה לכולה, אבל האי לא שייר מידי, דכל מה דחזי למעבד עבד:
Rashi on Gittin 43a:9:1.english: And if you say [that in the case of] "Half of you is betrothed to me," she is not betrothed - and you wish to resolve this [question] from it, that just as [when] one betroths half a woman, she is not betrothed — since we cannot say that he is saying to her that she may marry another alongside [him], for a woman is not fit for two [husbands], and thus it turns out that it is [only] half [of her] that he betrothed — so too here, [where] half a man betrothed [a woman], it is not a [valid] betrothal; [they are] not comparable, for there he left [something] out of his acquisition, since he should have betrothed all of her, whereas this one did not leave anything out, for everything that he is fit to do, he did:

Tosafot on Gittin 43a:6:1.hebrew: מי איכא עבדא דלא מזדבן לקנסא - וא"ת: כי אמר נמי דאינו מכור, תקשי ליה "מי איכא עבדא דלא מזדבן לקנסא", שיוכל למכרו כולו לגמרי! וי"ל: דלא ימצא קונים שיקנוהו לגמרי, אפי' לא יצטרכו לפרנסו, שיוכל לומר "עשה עמי ואיני זנך", מ"מ מימנעי אינשי לקנותו, שלא יהא רגיל אצלם; אבל אם מכרו לקנס מכור, זמנין דזבני ליה. ועי"ל: דאפי' מוכרו כולו לגמרי, אינו מכור, דהא אינו שוה כלום ואינו מוכרו אלא לקנס, ולקנס אינו מכור:
Tosafot on Gittin 43a:6:1.english: Is there a slave that cannot be sold with regard to the penalty - And if you will say: even if one says that [a slave sold only for the penalty] is not sold, [it] should [still] be difficult for him, "Is there a slave that cannot be sold with regard to the penalty?" — for he could sell him completely! And one can answer: he would not find buyers who would buy him completely; even though they would not need to sustain him, since [the buyer] could say [to him], "Work for me and I will not sustain you," nevertheless people refrain from buying him so that he will not be regularly around them. However, if [when] he sells him [only] for the penalty he is sold, there are times when they will buy him. And furthermore one can answer: even if he sells him completely, he is not sold, for he is worth nothing and he is only selling him for the penalty, and for the penalty he is not sold:

Tosafot on Gittin 43a:8:1.hebrew: אם תמצא לומר התקדשי לחציי מקודשת - וגבי אשה קאמר: אם תמצא לומר "חצייך מקודשת לי — אינה מקודשת". והוי מצי למימר איפכא, אלא האמת נקט, דהכי מסיק בפ"ק דקידושין (דף ז.):
Tosafot on Gittin 43a:8:1.english: If you say: Become betrothed to half of me, she is betrothed - And regarding a woman, [the Gemara] says: If you say, "Half of you is betrothed to me — she is not betrothed." Now, [the Gemara] could have stated the reverse, but it adopted the true [halakha], for so [the Gemara] concludes in the first chapter of Kiddushin (7a):
